title: bug: JetBrains STATE_SNAPSHOT project check deletes daemon.json and reconnects when a WSL-hosted daemon spells this project /mnt/<d>/...
description:
Found by architect-4ae016fb on 2026-10-30, while planning task-6fc0096b. It is the same bug class, one stage later: after the /health probe instead of before it.

What the code does
- MoeMessageDispatcher.handle, STATE_SNAPSHOT branch (moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeMessageDispatcher.kt, about lines 83-96), compares File(newState.project.rootPath).canonicalPath with File(project.basePath).canonicalPath.
- On a mismatch it deletes .moe/daemon.json unconditionally, then calls onProjectMismatch: disconnect, then scheduleReconnect.

Repro on Windows
- The project is D:/proj. A WSL agent's pre-flight started its daemon with --project /mnt/d/proj, so the snapshot's rootPath is /mnt/d/proj.
- On Windows, File('/mnt/d/proj').canonicalPath is D:\mnt\d\proj, so the check fails.
- The plugin deletes the live daemon.json and reconnects. The reconnect spawns a second daemon over the same .moe/.

After task-6fc0096b, readDaemonInfo, the reachability checks and the /health probe all accept that daemon as this project. This check is the one deleter left on that path.

Wanted
- Judge rootPath with task-6fc0096b's same-project rule, MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject: comparableProjectPath first, then canonicalPath. Do not add another normalizer.
- A genuinely different rootPath still disconnects and reconnects, as today.
- Remove daemon.json only through MoeDaemonSupervisor.deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged, against the DaemonInfo the client connected with, never unconditionally. The dispatcher holds no supervisor, so do the removal in MoeProjectService's onProjectMismatch.
- When planning, serialize with CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a): it also edits MoeProjectService.kt (restartDaemon).

Out of scope
- VS Code (task-80ed1fe8).
- restartDaemon.
definitionOfDone: A STATE_SNAPSHOT whose rootPath names this project in a drive, forward-slash, /mnt/<d> or //wsl$ spelling neither deletes daemon.json nor disconnects. A JetBrains test shows it.
A STATE_SNAPSHOT for another project still disconnects and reconnects. daemon.json is removed only while it still parses to the DaemonInfo the client connected with. Tests show both.
JetBrains tests pass under the jetbrains-gradle lease: from WSL, cmd.exe gradlew.bat test --rerun.

implementationPlan.description:
moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeMessageDispatcher.kt, the STATE_SNAPSHOT branch only.
- Keep the guard: a non-null basePath and a non-empty rootPath.
- Replace the two File(...).canonicalPath lines and their comparison with !MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(rootPath, basePath). That is task-6fc0096b's internal companion helper: comparableProjectPath first, canonicalPath as the fallback. Do not add another normalizer.
- On a mismatch: log.warn naming both raw paths, call onProjectMismatch(), and return.
- Delete the File(basePath, ".moe/daemon.json").delete() line. The dispatcher holds no supervisor and must never touch .moe/; MoeProjectService removes the file in step 3.
- Keep the java.io.IOException catch, because the canonical fallback can throw. As today, it skips the check.
- Drop the java.io.File import, which is now unused.
Nothing else in the file changes. The constructor and handle() signatures stay as they are, so every existing test that passes onProjectMismatch = {} compiles unchanged.

Error handling: unchanged. A null basePath, an empty rootPath or a canonical IOException skips the check and applies the state, as today.

Run the focused class. S1, S2, C1 and C3 go green. C2 stays red until step 3, because nothing removes the file yet.

moe-jetbrains/src/main/kotlin/com/moe/services/MoeProjectService.kt: remove daemon.json only through the compare-delete, against the DaemonInfo the client connected with.
1. Add `@Volatile private var clientDaemonInfo: DaemonInfo? = null` next to wsClient, with a one-line comment: the DaemonInfo the current wsClient was opened with.
2. In openClient, assign clientDaemonInfo = daemonInfo in the same wsLock block, on the line after wsClient = newClient. Nothing else writes it. It always belongs to the client that delivers a snapshot: onMessage drops a retired client's messages (wsClient !== this), and doConnect refuses while connected or connecting.
3. The constructor's onProjectMismatch lambda, in this order:
   - val info = clientDaemonInfo, read first;
   - disconnect(), as today;
   - when info != null, daemonSupervisor.deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(info). Log "Removed daemon.json naming the daemon on port <port>: it serves another project" when it returns true, and otherwise "Kept daemon.json: it no longer names that daemon", in handleForeignDaemon's style. Never File.delete, and never readDaemonInfo;
   - wsLock.withLock { isManualDisconnect = false } and scheduleReconnect(), as today.
4. Leave restartDaemon untouched (CQ-RF04 owns its post-stop delete and now dependsOn this task). Also leave handleForeignDaemon, connect, connectWithRetry and doConnect untouched.

Error handling: deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged never throws. It returns false on any IO, parse or delete failure, and on a blank base. A null info (no client was ever opened) deletes nothing and still reconnects. onProjectMismatch runs on the client's read thread, so keep disconnect()'s non-blocking close and never call closeBlocking there.

Run the focused class until S1, S2, C1, C2 and C3 all pass. Then run MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest and MoeProjectConnectionTest focused.

VERIFY ONCE, fresh. Edit only what this step's findings need, and report it in modifiedFiles.
1. Hold the jetbrains-gradle lease for every Gradle run (mem:convention-jetbrains-gradle-lease): moe.acquire_resource {resourceId: 'jetbrains-gradle', taskId, workerId, note}. If it is busy, call moe.report_blocked with resourceId 'jetbrains-gradle' and a reason that names no task id, because ids in a reason are parsed as blockers. Release the lease afterwards, even on failure.
2. Mutants, in a git-archive copy and never in the shared tree (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-qa-mutants-in-archive-copy):
   - Run git archive HEAD moe-jetbrains | tar -x -C /mnt/d/moe-scratch/task-007c0ea8/repo.
   - Overlay this task's 3 files and cmp-verify them.
   - Apply one mutant at a time with an exact-anchor replace, then run cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\moe-scratch\task-007c0ea8\repo\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --tests com.moe.services.MoeSnapshotProjectCheckTest --rerun".
   - Restore the file and cmp it.
   Each mutant must fail an assertion in the named rows; a compile error does not count.
   - M1, the dispatcher compares canonicalPath only (today's rule): S1's /mnt and WSL-share rows, and C1.
   - M2, the dispatcher's unconditional daemon.json delete is put back: S2 and C3.
   - M3, onProjectMismatch removes the file with File(basePath, ".moe/daemon.json").delete() instead of the compare-delete: C3.
   - M4, onProjectMismatch skips the removal: C2.
   - M5, onProjectMismatch drops scheduleReconnect(): C2 and C3.
   - M6, the dispatcher applies the state after onProjectMismatch (no return): S2 and C2.
3. The gate, on the shared tree, with the task's exact command:
   cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& cd /d D:\projexts\moes\moe-jetbrains && .\gradlew.bat test --rerun"
   - It must exit 0.
   - Count from the build/test-results/test/TEST-*.xml files dated after the gate start, not from the console. Report the totals with zero failures, errors and skips, and the counts for MoeSnapshotProjectCheckTest, MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest, MoeProjectConnectionTest, MoeDaemonSupervisorTest and both MoeMessageDispatcher test classes.
   - If a peer's red file or unresolved merge breaks the shared tree, follow mem:gotcha-jetbrains-shared-tree-gate-peer-red: get backup evidence from an archive copy with only this task's 3 files overlaid, then run the exact command on the shared tree once the peer is green. Never touch a peer's files.
   - If it exits 1 with 'Could not receive a message from the daemon', see mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-client-oom: check the Gradle daemon log, then rerun.
4. git diff --check over the two edited files must be clean, and the new test file must have no trailing whitespace. No git add, commit, stash or revert: the wrapper lands.
5. complete_task verification: that command, exit code 0 and the output tail, reported truthfully as Windows evidence. The summary maps DoD 1 to S1 and C1, DoD 2 to S2, C2 and C3, and DoD 3 to this gate. S1 is host-independent, and S2 and C1 derive their spellings from the host's own basePath, so CI's Linux run needs no change. Say that only Windows was run.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review. Read the 3-file diff two ways: as a user whose IDE and daemon sit on opposite sides of the Windows/WSL boundary, and as an attacker who controls .moe/daemon.json.
- Can a same-project rootPath in any spelling still reach a disconnect or a delete? Try drive letters, backslashes, forward slashes, case, a trailing separator, dot segments, /mnt/<d>, //wsl$ and //wsl.localhost.
- Does a same-project WSL-share spelling reach canonicalPath, which does network IO on Windows? It must not: comparableProjectPath decides first.
- Is daemon.json removed anywhere except through deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged against the client's DaemonInfo? Grep the diff for .delete( and readDaemonInfo.
- Concurrency:
  - a snapshot that arrives while disconnect() runs;
  - a second snapshot from the same client after the first mismatch (onMessage must drop it as retired);
  - a mismatch during Restart Daemon (the accepted race in planningNotes risks).
- A null basePath, an empty rootPath and a canonical IOException still skip the check, as today.
- Rails:
  - no .moe edits;
  - no Git writes;
  - none of the global rails' forbidden patterns;
  - error handling on every IO path, and a test for every behavior change.
- Would I be embarrassed if this shipped?
Fix any finding, then rerun step 4's gate fresh before complete_task.

Then write the Serena memory 'task-task-007c0ea856e546d2a619e012815cd89f-handoff' with the landed names, the rows, the mutants and the evidence. Update mem:gotcha-jetbrains-read-daemon-info-deletes: the dispatcher deleter is gone, and RF04's restart delete is the last unconditional one.

comments.content: @worker-5ebbf433 FYI from the governor (11:03Z): RF04 (task-de91373a, worker-73c29a03) is live too. It was claimed before its new dependsOn on this row existed. Its steps 1-2 touch only MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt and its test, so there's no overlap with you. Its step 3 edits MoeProjectService.kt, and I've asked it to stop at step 3 and report_blocked on this row until this row is DONE. You own MoeProjectService.kt until you land. If `git status` ever shows foreign hunks in it, don't edit over them; ping me.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: MoeMessageDispatcher judges a STATE_SNAPSHOT's project.rootPath with MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(rootPath, basePath): comparableProjectPath equality first, canonicalPath equality as the fallback. A rootPath naming this project in any Windows/WSL spelling (drive letter, backslash or forward slash, case, trailing separator, dot segments, /mnt/<d>, //wsl$, //wsl.localhost) applies the state, with no disconnect, no reconnect and no change to .moe/daemon.json. A rootPath naming another project disconnects and schedules the reconnect, as today. The dispatcher no longer touches .moe/. MoeProjectService's onProjectMismatch removes daemon.json only through deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged, against the DaemonInfo the current WebSocket client was opened with, so metadata that changed since connect survives byte for byte.
acceptanceCriteria: S1: every same-project spelling row gives zero onProjectMismatch calls and applies the snapshot's state.
S2: another project's rootPath, in its native and its other-side spelling, gives exactly one onProjectMismatch call, applies no state, and leaves daemon.json byte for byte.
C1: a live client that receives this project's other-side spelling stays connected, schedules no reconnect, applies the state, and leaves daemon.json unchanged.
C2: a live client that receives another project disconnects, schedules the reconnect, applies no state, and removes the daemon.json that still equals its DaemonInfo.
C3: when daemon.json changed in pid, port, startedAt or projectPath since connect, the mismatch still disconnects and reconnects, and the file survives byte for byte.
Mutants M1-M6 each fail an assertion in an archive copy, and the gate command exits 0 with fresh TEST-*.xml counts.
invariants: The dispatcher never reads, writes or deletes anything under .moe/.
On a project mismatch, daemon.json is removed only by deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(clientDaemonInfo). No File.delete is added anywhere.
comparableProjectPath stays the single cross-OS path rule; there is no second normalizer.
A null basePath, an empty rootPath or a canonical IOException skips the check and applies the state, as today.
restartDaemon, handleForeignDaemon, connect, connectWithRetry and doConnect behave as before.
compatibility: No wire change: the STATE_SNAPSHOT payload and every WebSocket and MCP message are unchanged.
MoeMessageDispatcher's constructor and handle(message) signatures are unchanged, so existing tests that pass onProjectMismatch = {} compile as they are.
Existing .moe/daemon.json files are read and compared exactly as task-6fc0096b's helpers already do.
approvedScope: MoeMessageDispatcher: the STATE_SNAPSHOT branch, and its now-unused java.io.File import.
MoeProjectService: the clientDaemonInfo field, its assignment in openClient, and the onProjectMismatch lambda.
New test class MoeSnapshotProjectCheckTest: rows S1, S2, C1, C2 and C3.
reuse: MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject and deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged from task-6fc0096b. There is no new normalizer, reader or deleter.

The test fixtures follow MoeProjectForeignDaemonTest (fake Project, reflection, an injected non-spawning supervisor, the other-side spelling helper) and MoeProjectConnectionTest (a loopback org.java_websocket server).
sourceAssumptions: MoeMessageDispatcher.handle, STATE_SNAPSHOT branch (about lines 80-103): it compares File(rootPath).canonicalPath with File(basePath).canonicalPath, deletes File(basePath, '.moe/daemon.json') unconditionally, then calls onProjectMismatch() and returns. An IOException skips the check.
MoeProjectService's constructor passes onProjectMismatch = { disconnect(); wsLock.withLock { isManualDisconnect = false }; scheduleReconnect() }.

MoeProjectService.openClient(daemonInfo) assigns wsClient = newClient inside wsLock, and onMessage ignores a client that is no longer wsClient. handleForeignDaemon already removes through deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(daemonInfo).
MoeDaemonSupervisor.Companion.isSameProject(path, base) and the instance method deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(expected): Boolean landed in c8a2a173 (task-6fc0096b, DONE).
packages/moe-daemon: STATE_SNAPSHOT project.rootPath is StateManager.projectPath, the daemon's raw --project, through normalizeProject in src/state/persistence.ts.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Give the dispatcher the supervisor or a delete callback. Rejected: the task puts the removal in MoeProjectService's onProjectMismatch, and keeping .moe IO out of the dispatcher keeps it a message router.
- Reread daemon.json at mismatch time (readDaemonInfo) and delete what it returns. Rejected: that compares the file with itself, not with the daemon the client connected to, so it would delete a newer daemon's metadata.
- Pass per-client context through handle(), as an extra parameter or a ThreadLocal. Rejected as more code than the problem needs. onMessage already drops a retired client's messages, so one field assigned with wsClient under wsLock is that client's DaemonInfo.
- Treat a relative rootPath as unknown, as /health's classify does. Out of scope: the daemon writes the same raw --project into daemon.json, and readDaemonInfo already refuses such metadata before any snapshot arrives. Raise a follow-up if a real case appears.
- Also publish handleForeignDaemon's 'serves another project' status here. Rejected: the DoD keeps today's disconnect and reconnect, with no UX change.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- After task-6fc0096b, readDaemonInfo, isReachable and the /health probe all accept a same-project Windows/WSL spelling. The STATE_SNAPSHOT check is the last deleter on the connect path. restartDaemon's post-stop delete belongs to CQ-RF04 (task-de91373a), which now dependsOn this task.
- The daemon's STATE_SNAPSHOT project.rootPath is its raw --project: StateManager.projectPath, through normalizeProject in packages/moe-daemon/src/state/persistence.ts. A WSL daemon spells it /mnt/<d>/..., and on Windows File('/mnt/d/proj').canonicalPath is D:\mnt\d\proj.
- MoeDaemonSupervisor.isSameProject(path, base) is an internal companion helper: comparableProjectPath equality first, canonicalPath equality second. internal is visible from the test source set (mem:gotcha-kotlin-internal-visible-from-test-sourceset).
- deleteDaemonInfoIfUnchanged(expected) does a bounded reread, compares all four DaemonInfo fields, never throws, and refuses a blank base.
- onMessage checks wsClient !== this under wsLock, and doConnect refuses while connected or connecting, so the client that delivers a snapshot is the one openClient last assigned.
- onProjectMismatch runs on the client's read thread. disconnect() closes that client from its own thread, as today.
- WSL has no JDK. The JetBrains gate runs through cmd.exe gradlew.bat under the jetbrains-gradle lease (mem:gotcha-jetbrains-gradle-from-wsl).
planningNotes.risks:
- Windows TEMP may hold 8.3 names. Derive every spelling from the exact basePath string handed to the fake project.
- Never let a //wsl$ or UNC spelling reach canonicalPath on a Windows host: that does network IO on the WSL share. The other-side helper yields /mnt/<d> on Windows, so S2 and C1 stay local. The red run on today's code does canonicalize S1's literal bases, which is why they name paths that cannot exist.
- Accepted race: Restart Daemon could disconnect, restart and open a new client while a retired client's read thread is stalled inside a mismatch. The mismatch path would then read the new client's DaemonInfo. That needs a stall across a whole restart, and it is the same best-effort class as the compare-delete's TOCTOU, which task-6fc0096b already accepted.
- A reconnect fires 5 s after a mismatch. The fixture injects a supervisor whose starter throws, and disposes in finally.
- The shared tree compiles peers' in-progress .kt files. Hold the lease while your red file is in the tree, and put mutants in an archive copy only.
- RF04 rebases onto this task's MoeProjectService.kt bytes; restartDaemon stays untouched here.

blockedReason: Waiting for the shared jetbrains-gradle lease, held by another worker's red/green and gate runs. Step 1's test file is drafted in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/task-007c0ea8 and cannot enter the shared tree or run until the lease is mine.
